metadata.title: IDScan.net breach (Sep 2026): ~153M driver's licenses on the dark web — the digital-ID honeypot, realized (incl. the SecDef/'Secretary of War')
metadata.frame: The single clearest live validation of this project's digital-ID HONEYPOT argument (digitalid-orchestration 'honeypot_realized_live_cases', and the antidote-architecture): centralize the population's identity documents at one private verification vendor, and one breach exposes everyone at once - including the highest-access officials. A dark-web service ('Nexus', advertised on the Russian cybercrime forum Exploit, Aug 31 2026; surfaced by Brian Krebs Sep 1) offered ~153M US/Canada driver's-license scans + ~10M ID cards + ~3M travel docs + ~579k medical cards (claimed ~170M+ people). The FBI (New Orleans) is investigating; the suspected source is Louisiana ID-verification firm IDScan.net (~21M verifications/mo).
metadata.grade: REPORTED (Krebs/KrebsOnSecurity + multiple outlets; FBI investigating). IDScan.net has NOT confirmed the breach and figures are not independently verified => attribution-to-IDScan and exact counts graded 'reported/uncorroborated-by-the-firm'. The honeypot INTERPRETATION is this project's thesis, labeled.
metadata.why_it_matters: It proves the structural objection the ID-proponents wave away: aggregation is the risk. Front-and-back scans (some incl. IR/UV captures), Common Access Cards, employment-authorization + residence cards, and 'continuously exfiltrated for over a year' near-real-time = catastrophic even WITHOUT quantum (the plain stolen-outright case macro-pqc-chips's PQC 'escape hatch' does not fix). Physical-safety crisis for DV survivors / witness-protection / and for officials like the Secretary of War.
metadata.method: KrebsOnSecurity; TechCrunch 2026-09-02; Engadget; Cybernews; Malwarebytes; Yahoo/Protos (Hegseth listing). Common victim link reported = Hertz rentals (IDScan clients incl. Hertz, Target, FedEx, Caesars, Motorola, Jack Henry).

edges.notes: IDScan.net = centralized ID-verification vendor (~21M+ verifications/month for Fortune-500 clients) - i.e., a single aggregation point holding front/back license scans: the honeypot the digital-ID critique warns about (fact of business model).

'Nexus' dark-web service (advertised on Russian forum Exploit, Aug 31 2026) claimed to have 'continuously exfiltrated new data for over a year' with near-real-time access (~500k docs/day added) from 'a major identity-verification company'; Krebs + reporting point to IDScan; site shuttered after publicity (reported; IDScan not confirmed).
Common thread among victims = Hertz car rentals (IDScan verifies renters); other named clients: Target, FedEx, Caesars, Motorola, Jack Henry - the aggregation footprint (reported).

The listing included US Secretary of Defense / 'Secretary of War' Pete Hegseth's driver's license (offered ~$100), previewed to Krebs - plus Common Access Cards, employment-authorization + residence cards. A high-access official's ID in a mass leak is the acute national-security case (reported).
Hegseth heads the Department of War (renamed from DoD, 2025) - so his exposed ID sits atop the defense/Palantir-Maven/Anduril stack (fact of role).

This IS the 'honeypot realized' scenario the antidote-architecture argues against - centralization guarantees single-point catastrophic exposure; PQC does NOT fix plain exfiltration (cross-ref digitalid-orchestration, macro-pqc-chips) (interpretation, labeled; the breach is reported fact).
